title: Astronomy — Pictor Nebula
prompt:
Listen to an audio passage, answer all multiple-select questions, then rate passage and question difficulty.

This is the stimuli:
Transcript:
About four thousand light-years away from Earth sits the Pictor Nebula. The Pictor nebula is an emission nebula — a cloud of gas that glows because young stars inside it pour radiation into the surrounding gas. Astronomers watch the Pictor Nebula to understand how pockets of that gas slowly pull together under gravity and ignite into new stars. They observe this process with an optical telescope, tuned to red light.

Images of the nebula tend to leave a strong impression, even on people who don't usually pay much attention to astronomy. The colors and shapes seem almost too vivid to be real, though they're exactly what the telescope captures. It's the kind of sight that makes clear why so many people find deep-sky objects captivating.

Questions:
Question 1: Which of the following correctly describe the Pictor Nebula? Select all that apply. 1) It is a cloud of gas 2) It is located about four thousand light-years from Earth 3) It is lit from within by young stars 4) It is a dense ball of old stars 5) None of the above
Question 2: How do scientists observe the Pictor Nebula? Select all that apply. 1) With an optical telescope 2) By picking up red light emitted by the nebula 3) Using radio equipment that picks up regular pulses 4) By measuring how its mass varies over time 5) None of the above
Question 3: What do astronomers study the Pictor Nebula to learn? Select all that apply. 1) How gravity pulls pockets of gas together 2) How gas clouds ignite into new stars 3) How gravitational waves ripple through a region of space 4) How black hole emissions change 5) None of the above
Question 4: Which of the following correctly describes the Pictor Nebula? Select all that apply. 1) A gas cloud lit by embedded young stars that is studied to understand how new stars form 2) A gas cloud lit by embedded young stars that is studied to understand gravitational waves 3) The remains of a dying star that is studied to understand how new stars form 4) The remains of a dying star that is studied to understand gravitational waves 5) None of the above
Question 5: Which of the following correctly identifies what the Pictor Nebula is? Select all that apply. 1) An emission nebula — a dense ball of old stars gravitationally bound together 2) A globular pulsar — a cloud of gas lit by its own embedded young stars 3) A globular pulsar — the collapsed core of an exploded massive star 4) An emission nebula — two stars in a close gravitational orbit 5) None of the above

On a scale 1-10, rate how difficult the passage was, and how difficult the questions were.

Give your response according to the following formatting rules:
Output ONLY lines in this exact format:
Question 1: 1,3
Question 2: 2
...
Passage Difficulty: 7
Question Difficulty: 7
(List every correct option number for a question, separated by commas. If none apply, use the "None of the above" option number.)
